title: Server error (5xx)
clarifying: How many URLs share this reason (single, cluster, sitewide)?
When was the last crawl attempt on the affected URLs?
Are these URLs in a submitted sitemap?
structure: GSC signals: URL Inspection.pageFetchState=SERVER_ERROR + lastCrawlTime. Split by blast radius (count of affected URLs) and recency of lastCrawlTime. All terminals are recommendations to infra/backend team — no direct fix in this workflow.

nodes.label: Server error (5xx)
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState + lastCrawlTime for each affected URL
Page Indexing report: count of URLs with this reason
Analyze URL patterns — same path prefix? Same subdomain?
S1. Blast radius?
S2. lastCrawlTime recency?
SUGGEST: Single URL, recent — share URL + timestamp with backend team; ask for app-log review at that timestamp
SUGGEST: Single URL, old — request URL Inspection live test; error may already be resolved
SUGGEST: Cluster on same path pattern — flag section-specific dependency (backend service, DB, template) to eng team
SUGGEST: Sitewide — escalate to infra/DevOps; likely host availability, CDN/WAF, or deployment issue; share Crawl Stats host-status export

title: Redirect error
clarifying: How many URLs have this reason?
Do the affected URLs share a domain/subdomain flip pattern?
Are they in the sitemap?
structure: GSC API reports the state but not the redirect chain itself. Workflow branches on affected-URL count and URL-pattern analysis, and always terminates in a suggestion for the team to trace the chain externally.

nodes.label: Redirect error
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState=REDIRECT_ERROR
Page Indexing report: URL list + count
Look for shared prefix, protocol/subdomain flip, or www/non-www variants
S1. Pattern across affected URLs?
SUGGEST: Protocol/subdomain flip pattern detected — instruct eng to enforce one canonical host+scheme with a single 301 at the edge
SUGGEST: Cluster on same path — instruct eng to trace redirect chain (curl -IL) for one sample URL; likely template-level loop or chain
SUGGEST: Single URL — instruct team to trace redirect chain externally; typical fixes are collapsing to a single 301 to final URL

title: URL blocked by robots.txt
clarifying: Is the URL in a submitted sitemap (indicates intent to index)?
Is the URL indexed via external links (coverageState = Indexed, though blocked)?
Any Search Analytics impressions on the URL?
structure: Use Sitemaps API to detect intent conflict, and URL Inspection.coverageState to check whether the URL is still surfacing in Search via external links. Recommendation depends on intent conflict.

nodes.label: URL blocked by robots.txt
URL Inspection API: robotsTxtState=DISALLOWED, coverageState
Sitemaps API: is this URL in a submitted sitemap?
S1. In sitemap?
S2. Indexed anyway via external links?
SUGGEST: Conflict: URL in sitemap AND blocked by robots.txt. Decide intent — if you want it indexed, ask team to remove the Disallow rule; if not, ask team to remove URL from sitemap
HANDOFF: R16 Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt
SUGGEST: Not in sitemap, not indexed — treat as intentional; no action needed. If unintentional, ask team to remove the Disallow rule

title: URL marked 'noindex'
clarifying: Where is the noindex signal (BLOCKED_BY_META_TAG vs BLOCKED_BY_HTTP_HEADER)?
Is the URL in a submitted sitemap?
Is it also disallowed in robots.txt (would prevent Googlebot from seeing a noindex removal)?
structure: URL Inspection.indexingState distinguishes meta tag vs HTTP header. Sitemap presence signals unintended noindex. Robots.txt conflict flag surfaces a common mistake.

nodes.label: URL marked 'noindex'
URL Inspection API: indexingState + robotsTxtState
Sitemaps API: is URL in a submitted sitemap?
S1. Source of noindex?
S2. In sitemap?
S3. Also blocked by robots.txt?
SUGGEST: noindex meta tag on a sitemap URL — ask eng to remove <meta name='robots' content='noindex'> from page template
SUGGEST: X-Robots-Tag: noindex header on a sitemap URL — ask eng/DevOps to remove header at server or CDN level
SUGGEST: noindex AND robots.txt Disallow both present — ask team to remove robots.txt Disallow first, otherwise Googlebot cannot see any future noindex change
SUGGEST: Not in sitemap — likely intentional noindex; no action unless you expected this URL in Search

title: Soft 404
clarifying: Is the URL in a submitted sitemap?
Do multiple URLs in the same section share this reason (template issue)?
Does the URL have Search Analytics history (was it ever ranking)?
structure: Split by sitemap membership + cluster pattern. All terminals suggest content or status-code review — the workflow doesn't perform the review.

nodes.label: Soft 404
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState=SOFT_404
Sitemaps API: URL in sitemap?
Search Analytics API: any impressions/clicks last 90d?
Group affected URLs by path prefix / template
S1. Cluster on shared template?
S2. In sitemap AND had traffic?
SUGGEST: Section-wide soft-404 — ask team to audit the template (empty categories, out-of-stock, JS-render failure)
SUGGEST: Sitemap URL with past traffic — ask team to restore content or 301 to the closest replacement
SUGGEST: Sitemap URL, no traffic — ask team to remove from sitemap and return a real 404/410
SUGGEST: Not in sitemap, no clear pattern — ask team to audit whether URL should exist; if yes, add real content; if no, return 404/410

title: Blocked due to unauthorized request (401)
clarifying: Are ALL URLs on the property 401 or just a subset?
Is the domain a staging URL that shouldn't be verified in GSC?
Any URLs in the sitemap 401'ing (implies intent to be public)?
structure: First check: is the entire property 401 (staging property mistakenly verified)? Otherwise identify subset pattern.

nodes.label: Blocked due to unauthorized request (401)
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState=BLOCKED_4XX (401)
Page Indexing report: what share of URLs are 401?
Sitemaps API: any 401'd URLs in a submitted sitemap?
S1. Scope?
SUGGEST: Nearly all URLs 401 — GSC property likely points at a staging/preview domain; ask team to verify the production property instead and remove staging
SUGGEST: Sitemap URLs 401'ing — ask team to either make those URLs public or remove them from the sitemap
SUGGEST: Subset of URLs 401 — ask security/backend team to review auth wall on those paths; verify Googlebot is not being blocked by intent

title: Not found (404)
clarifying: Was the URL previously indexed (Search Analytics history)?
Is it in a submitted sitemap?
Any inbound external links (URL Inspection referring URLs)?
structure: Route by past value + sitemap intent. A 404 is often correct; only worth escalating when the URL had traffic, is still submitted, or has external links pointing at it.

nodes.label: Not found (404)
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState=NOT_FOUND + referringUrls
Search Analytics API: impressions/clicks last 90d
Sitemaps API: URL in sitemap?
S1. Has traffic history OR external links?
S2. In sitemap?
SUGGEST: High-value URL (traffic or links) — ask team to 301 to closest replacement URL
SUGGEST: URL 404s but is still in sitemap — ask team to remove from sitemap OR restore/redirect
SUGGEST: No traffic, no links, not in sitemap — safe to leave as 404 (or 410 for a stronger signal); no urgent action

title: Blocked due to access forbidden (403)
clarifying: What share of URLs are 403 (sitewide vs subset)?
Any recent WAF/CDN deploy visible in Crawl Stats?
Is the URL in a sitemap?
structure: GSC surfaces the state; the API cannot tell you which WAF rule fires. Terminals hand the URL list to infra/security for review.

nodes.label: Blocked due to access forbidden (403)
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState=ACCESS_DENIED
Page Indexing report: 403 count vs total
Sitemaps API: any 403'd URLs in sitemap?
S1. Scope?
SUGGEST: Sitewide 403 — ask security/infra to check WAF/CDN rules blocking verified Googlebot; provide GSC's Googlebot IP verification pattern
SUGGEST: 403 on sitemap URLs — flag as blocking indexing intent; escalate to security with the URL list
SUGGEST: Subset of URLs 403 — provide list to security team; possible path-specific ACL or geo-restriction

title: URL blocked due to other 4xx issue
clarifying: What is the exact HTTP status (GSC API buckets this)?
Is the URL in a sitemap?
Any pattern in the affected URLs?
structure: GSC does not disclose the exact 4xx sub-code here. The suggestion is always to expose the specific status externally and share the list with the responsible team.

nodes.label: URL blocked due to other 4xx issue
URL Inspection API: pageFetchState=BLOCKED_4XX
Page Indexing report: URL list
Sitemaps API: any of these in sitemap?
S1. In sitemap?
SUGGEST: Sitemap URLs affected — ask team to run HTTP-status audit on this URL list and reveal the specific 4xx (429 / 410 / 400 / 451). Priority = high
SUGGEST: Not in sitemap — provide URL list to backend team for HTTP-status audit; likely 429 (rate limit) or 410 (intentional gone)

title: Crawled — currently not indexed
clarifying: How long has the URL been in this state (lastCrawlTime)?
What share of the site has this reason?
Do affected URLs have Search Analytics impressions elsewhere?
structure: Age gate first — <14d is normal. Then split single-URL quality review vs sitewide pattern.

nodes.label: Crawled — currently not indexed
URL Inspection API: coverageState + lastCrawlTime + userCanonical/googleCanonical
Page Indexing report: URL count / share
Search Analytics API: impressions in last 90d
S1. Time since lastCrawlTime?
S2. Share of site affected?
SUGGEST: <14 days since crawl — too early to act; monitor
SUGGEST: Large share of site affected — sitewide quality signal; recommend content-quality audit and content-strategy review with editorial team
SUGGEST: Subset of URLs — recommend per-URL content-quality audit: depth, uniqueness vs canonical, internal linking, template differentiation
SUGGEST: >90 days in this state — URL has failed the quality bar; recommend consolidation, redirect to canonical, or removal

title: Discovered — currently not indexed
clarifying: Is host status healthy in Crawl Stats?
What's the total URL count on the property?
Are many affected URLs parametric/faceted?
structure: First check host health (a slow/overloaded server is the biggest cause). Then split by site size and URL pattern (faceted bloat vs low authority).

nodes.label: Discovered — currently not indexed
URL Inspection API: coverageState='Discovered - currently not indexed'
Crawl Stats API: host availability + response time
Page Indexing report: total URL count on property
Scan affected URLs for query params, session IDs, faceted patterns
S1. Host healthy?
HANDOFF: R1 Server error (server unhealthy)
S2. Site size + URL pattern?
SUGGEST: Slow TTFB in Crawl Stats — recommend server-performance work with infra: cache/CDN/DB tuning
SUGGEST: Faceted/parametric URLs dominating discovery — recommend canonicalizing params, disallowing infinite param combos in robots.txt, curating the sitemap
SUGGEST: Small site, clean URLs — recommend strengthening internal linking to affected URLs and building external links to raise authority

title: Alternate page with proper canonical tag
clarifying: Does userCanonical equal googleCanonical for this URL?
Is the canonical URL itself indexed?
Is this an hreflang language variant?
structure: Almost always expected. Only escalates when canonical target isn't indexed, or when this fires on an hreflang variant that should be independently indexed.

nodes.label: Alternate page with proper canonical tag
URL Inspection API: userCanonical, googleCanonical, verdict
URL Inspection API on canonical URL: coverageState
S1. Canonical mismatch?
S2. Canonical URL indexed?
S3. Is this an hreflang variant?
HANDOFF: R14 Duplicate, Google chose different canonical
SUGGEST: Working as expected — no action needed
SUGGEST: Canonical target isn't indexed — pivot investigation to the target URL's indexing reason
SUGGEST: Hreflang locale variant treated as alternate — ask team to audit hreflang cluster; language variants should each be independently indexable, not consolidated

title: Duplicate without user-selected canonical
clarifying: Are affected URLs parametric, protocol variants, or trailing-slash variants?
Is Google's chosen canonical indexed?
Are these truly duplicates or should they be distinct?
structure: Pattern-detect the duplication source (params / protocol / slash / case) and recommend the matching normalization. If pages should be distinct, recommend content differentiation.

nodes.label: Duplicate without user-selected canonical
URL Inspection API: userCanonical=null, googleCanonical present
Compare affected URL vs Google's canonical — identify diff (query param, protocol, slash, case)
S1. What causes the duplication?
SUGGEST: Query-parameter duplicates — recommend adding rel=canonical to param-free URL, and reviewing tracking-param policy
SUGGEST: HTTP/HTTPS or WWW/non-WWW variants — recommend edge-level 301 to preferred host+scheme
SUGGEST: Trailing-slash variants — recommend normalization: pick one form and 301 the other
SUGGEST: URL case variants — recommend 301 to lowercase (or configure server to be case-insensitive)
SUGGEST: Pages should be distinct — recommend content-differentiation work with editorial team

title: Duplicate, Google chose different canonical than user
clarifying: What did Google pick (googleCanonical)?
Are declared and Google-selected canonicals content-equivalent?
Any hreflang cluster involving these URLs?
structure: Diagnose why Google overrode: content dissimilarity vs conflicting signals vs authority gap vs hreflang misconfig.

nodes.label: Duplicate, Google chose different canonical than user
URL Inspection API: userCanonical, googleCanonical
Sitemaps API: is chosen canonical in sitemap?
Cross-check: sitemap, hreflang, internal-link count (via Links report)
S1. Signal-alignment status?
SUGGEST: Conflicting signals (sitemap says X, canonical tag says Y) — ask team to align sitemap, canonical tag, and internal links on the intended URL
SUGGEST: Chosen canonical has stronger external+internal signals — either accept Google's pick (update your canonical to match) or invest in strengthening the intended URL
SUGGEST: Hreflang cluster misconfigured — ask team to audit hreflang self-references and locale codes
SUGGEST: Declared canonical too dissimilar to the page — either align content or drop the declared canonical

title: Page with redirect
clarifying: Which URL should be indexed — source or target?
Is the redirect target itself indexed?
Are affected URLs in the sitemap (implies you want THEM indexed)?
structure: Usually expected. Escalates when the source URL is in the sitemap (contradiction), or when the redirect target isn't indexed.

nodes.label: Page with redirect
URL Inspection API on source URL: pageFetchState + redirect target
Sitemaps API: is source URL in sitemap?
URL Inspection API on target URL: coverageState
S1. Source URL in sitemap?
S2. Target URL indexed?
SUGGEST: Source URL is in sitemap but redirects away — ask team to either remove the redirect at origin OR remove source URL from sitemap and add the target instead
SUGGEST: Target URL isn't indexed — pivot investigation to the target's indexing reason
SUGGEST: Working as expected — no action needed

title: Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt
clarifying: Do you want this URL in Search or not?
Any sensitive content on the URL that requires urgent removal?
structure: Two-branch decision on intent. If content is sensitive, add an urgent-removal recommendation.

nodes.label: Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt
URL Inspection API: coverageState='Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt'
S1. Intent?
SUGGEST: Wants URL OUT of Search — ask team to (a) remove robots.txt Disallow so Googlebot can crawl, (b) add noindex meta or header. Robots.txt alone will NOT drop it from the index
SUGGEST: Wants URL IN Search — ask team to remove the robots.txt Disallow so Googlebot can crawl and produce proper snippets
SUGGEST: Sensitive content — recommend GSC Removals tool for immediate temporary block (6 months), then apply noindex per the OUT-of-Search flow

title: Page indexed without content
clarifying: Does the rendered HTML in URL Inspection screenshot show content or a blank page?
Is the raw HTML empty as well?
Any indication of geo/UA-specific serving?
structure: URL Inspection returns the rendered HTML + screenshot. Branch on rendered vs raw vs both.

nodes.label: Page indexed without content
URL Inspection API: rendered HTML + screenshot + HTTP response
S1. What does Googlebot see?
SUGGEST: Raw HTML has content, rendered HTML empty — client-side rendering issue; ask eng team to add SSR/prerender or expose content in raw HTML
SUGGEST: Different content served to Googlebot vs users — cloaking flag; ask team to serve identical content
SUGGEST: Both raw and rendered HTML empty — page has no content; ask editorial team to add substantive content
SUGGEST: Content in unsupported format (image-only, PDF-in-iframe, Flash) — ask team to expose visible content as HTML text

title: Blocked by Page Removal tool
clarifying: Is there an active Removals request for this URL?
Who submitted it (property owner audit)?
Should the URL be back in Search?
structure: Query Removals API for active requests; branch on intent.

nodes.label: Blocked by Page Removal tool
GSC Removals API: active requests for URL
S1. Removal intended?
SUGGEST: Unintended — cancel the Removals request in GSC; requester should be identified via property-access audit
SUGGEST: Intended — no action; request expires in ~6 months

title: Blocked due to legal issue
clarifying: Are you the rightful content owner?
Is documentation available to file a counter-notice?
structure: Not a technical fix. Route to legal review.

nodes.label: Blocked due to legal issue
URL Inspection API confirms legal-blocked state
S1. Rightful owner with documentation?
SUGGEST: Escalate to legal team — file a counter-notice via Google Legal Removals (or the applicable regional process)
SUGGEST: Not rightful owner OR no documentation — legal review outside SEO scope; track resolution date

Where does the noindex signal originate?
structure: Legacy label with the same underlying signal as R4. Handoff to R4 workflow.

nodes.label: Excluded by 'noindex' tag (legacy)
HANDOFF: R4 URL marked 'noindex' — use that workflow

title: Master router — "Audit this content"

meta.handoffs: CA1, CA2, CA3, CA4, CA5, CA6, CA7, CA8, TECH

clarifying: Is this a single-URL audit or a whole-library pass?
Is the page even live and indexable before auditing content quality?
structure: Picks the dominant content problem for a URL (or triggers the library-balance pass), then routes to the specialist module. Gate first: if the page can't be served/indexed, that's a technical fix — hand off, don't audit content on a page that can't rank.

S0. Scope?
S0a. Live & indexable? (200, not noindex, canonical-self)

clarifying: Does this page have meaningful traffic or strategic/BOFU value?
Is it performing to its potential, or underperforming?

ACTION: re-angle to matching type (comparison page, use-case, pricing) or spin off a new matching asset

ACTION: brief MOFU/BOFU first — 'best X for [use case]', 'X vs Y', 'how to choose', pricing/ROI, case studies
TERMINAL: intent OK — continue to CA4 structure

title: ICP alignment (5 dimensions)
clarifying: Does the ranking query attract the right ICP role or segment?

structure:
Linear pre-setup spine (PO -> contract/SOW -> scope lock -> internal kickoff), then a
branch by SOW nature into up to three parallel service-line checklists (SEO/GEO, Social,
Video), each a sequential chain of six grouped checkpoints. All branches converge on the
client kickoff call, then terminate by handing the account into the live RAG dashboard.
Any checkpoint left unresolved at handoff is designed to surface as a Yellow flag in the
first monitoring cycle rather than silently passing through.
rationale: Built from the account onboarding workflow discussion: PO receipt and contract/SOW signing are gate conditions, not just paperwork steps, because Pepper has at least one live account (Flipkart) where the PO is the sole governing document with no separate addendum. The service-line branch exists because a single SOW may cover any combination of SEO/GEO, Social, and Video, and each has materially different setup requirements. Checkpoints are grouped (rather than one node per individual checklist item) to keep the tree navigable; the full item-level detail for each checkpoint lives in the account onboarding checklist doc and should be linked from each node in the app.
